description: Provides comprehensive coverage of computational linguistics, neural language models, sequence-to-sequence transformers, and Large Language Model fine-tuning.
learning_objectives: Understand linguistic preprocessing, n-gram statistical language models, and distributed word vectors.
Implement sequence models for Named Entity Recognition, POS tagging, and sentiment classification.
Master Transformer architectures, self-attention mechanisms, BERT, and GPT models.
Fine-tune and evaluate Large Language Models using prompt engineering, LoRA, and PEFT.
outline: NLP Fundamentals: Tokenization, morphology, POS tagging, lemmatization, N-gram language models, perplexity.
Word Embeddings: Word2Vec (Skip-gram, CBOW), GloVe, FastText, subword tokenization (BPE, WordPiece).
Sequence Modeling: Hidden Markov Models (HMM), Conditional Random Fields (CRF), RNNs, LSTMs for text classification.
Attention & Transformers: Encoder-Decoder models, self-attention, Multi-Head Attention, Transformer architecture (BERT, T5, GPT).
Modern LLM Engineering: Pre-training, fine-tuning (LoRA, PEFT), prompt engineering, text generation evaluation (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR).

books.title: Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing
books.author: Christopher D. Manning, Hinrich Schütze
